analysis.title: Asia Open - The beat goes on
key_insights: Risk-on tone returned after SpaceX's earnings and projections reinforced confidence in the durability of the AI capex cycle. Risk remains sensitive to geopolitical headlines, including Washington ordering US embassy personnel back to Saudi Arabia and new tri-lateral diplomacy efforts in the Russo-Ukraine war.
SPX rose 0.58% and NDX rose 1.13%, with momentum flows on the desk going back into semis. Breadth weakened, with advancers and decliners nearly split.
Both SPX and NDX closed back above key CTA levels, which would see systematic funds adding back longs into Thursday's session.
Derivatives showed demand for downside hedges despite subdued vols, mainly through put spreads across SPX and ES.

Meta rose about 5% after hours. Q3 revenue grew 26% and 4Q revenue guidance cleared the high end of the buyside bar of $76bn. Meta gave no 2027 fiscal-year outlook and raised the low end of its capex range by $5bn to $135bn, with the top end unchanged at $145bn.

Texas Instruments (-1%) posted a beat with gross margin upside, helped by automotive and industrial demand. Revenue was $6.3bn. IBM (+3%) reported sales of $17.1bn vs $16.82bn expected, with adjusted EPS of $2.95.

UST yields rose in a bear-flattening move, with the front end and belly leading the selloff. Front-end US yields rose 3bps, and +4bps of Fed pricing sits in one week before the October FOMC. The long bond was roughly flat at 5.415%.
The $13bn 20-year reopening tailed the 1pm market level by 0.9bp, at a 5.469% yield. Bid/cover was 2.73, the 73rd percentile of the past 12 auctions.
In Europe, UK gilts rallied despite hotter-than-expected CPI. The OAT-Bund spread widened to over 160bps, with OATs underperforming Bunds.

USDMXN rose 1.3% to 18.66, a one-year high, with no clear catalyst and retail sales of +1.2% MoM well above expectations. Desk flows were real-money and corporate outflows, and the Citi trader is bearish MXN into Thursday's CPI.
FX flows skewed toward EM and high-beta currencies, with leveraged buying in CNH, SEK and ZAR. TRY and MXN saw the largest net outflows. The dollar was little changed overall and weaker against G10.

Commodities gave mixed signals. Brent and WTI diverged, with Brent supported by concerns over Gulf supply disruptions and the Brent-WTI spread widening. Natural gas fell 6.0% on profit-taking after yesterday's surge above €90.
New Zealand Q3 CPI is due at 22:45 BST. Citi expects 0.8% QoQ and 3.9% YoY, versus 1.5% and 4.1% prior, in line with RBNZ forecasts. Upside risks remain for a higher terminal OCR.

Citi economists expect the BSP to raise its policy rate by 25bp to 5.25%. They expect the BoK to hold at 3.00% with a hawkish bias, after back-to-back summer hikes, and see 25bp hikes in November 2026 and February 2027 toward a 3.5% terminal rate.
Citi's traders are looking for dip opportunities to add AUD exposure via AUDNZD ahead of New Zealand CPI.
